tasks.gr9-electricity-electric-cells-t3: Topic: Electricity and Electric Cells. Cover electric current, circuits, power source, load, conductors, series vs parallel circuits, potential difference (voltage), and resistance. Ask learners to identify circuit parts, predict brightness changes, distinguish series from parallel, or explain how voltage and resistance affect current.
tasks.gr9-heat-energy-transfer-t3: Topic: Heat and Energy Transfer. Cover conduction, convection, radiation, insulators, exothermic and endothermic reactions, temperature, and energy conservation. Ask learners to identify heat transfer methods, explain insulation, classify reactions, or apply principles to everyday scenarios.
tasks.gr9-forces-t3: Topic: Forces (Grade 9 Natural Sciences, Term 3). Cover a force as a push, pull or twist measured in newtons (N), what a force can change (shape, direction, speed), forces acting in pairs, contact forces (friction, tension, compression) versus field forces (gravitational, magnetic, electrostatic), gravity and weight: weight = mass x g with g = 10 N/kg (always give g in the question), mass stays the same but weight changes on the Moon (about one sixth), magnets (north and south poles, like repel, unlike attract, magnetic substances iron steel cobalt nickel, the Earth's magnetic field), electrostatic force by rubbing (only electrons move; like charges repel, unlike attract) and lightning as a discharge of charge with safety precautions. Describe any situation in words and numbers (there is no picture). Ask Grade 9 learners to identify, explain and calculate.
tasks.gr9-electricity-safety-t3: Topic: Safety with Electricity (Grade 9 Natural Sciences, Term 3). Cover fuses (wire melts, breaks the circuit when the current is too big), circuit breakers (trip and can be switched back on), earth leakage, the 3-pin plug (live, neutral, earth) and earthing (earth wire joined to the metal case and to an earth cable in the ground with almost zero resistance), overload in parallel circuits (total current is the sum of the branch currents; compare with the rating of the breaker, which is always given), the plan for wiring a house (each room its own light with a switch; main switch and fuse) and illegal connections to the Eskom supply as energy theft. Do not ask for wire colours or fuse ratings. Ask Grade 9 learners to explain and calculate.
